scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for this person to test their boyfriend by changing their appearance and behavior. Let me break this down step by step. First, the person is a model and has had past relationships where guys were more interested in her looks and status than her as a person. That's caused her a lot of anxiety and depression, so she's really looking for someone who cares about her beyond her looks. She's currently dating someone who seems genuine, supportive, and interested in her hobbies, which is a good sign. But then her boyfriend's friend messaged her, saying that her boyfriend has been bragging about their intimate life to others, which is concerning. She's considering testing her boyfriend by not wearing makeup and avoiding physical intimacy for a month to see if he still wants to be with her. She's torn between feeling like this is necessary to confirm his true motives and worrying that it's manipulative or unfair. On one hand, she's been hurt before, and she wants to ensure that this relationship is different. Testing him could give her the peace of mind she needs. It's a way to verify whether his interest in her is genuine or just based on her looks and status. If he still wants to be with her without the external factors, that could confirm that he cares about her as a person. On the other hand, this approach might be manipulative. Relationships should be built on trust and mutual respect, not on tests. If she starts avoiding intimacy or changing her appearance, it could create unnecessary tension and make her boyfriend feel insecure or confused. It might also lead to resentment if he doesn't understand why she's acting this way. Another consideration is communication. Instead of testing him, maybe she should talk to him about her concerns. Open and honest communication is key in any relationship. If she expresses her fears and insecurities, he might be able to reassure her without her needing to resort to testing. This approach could strengthen their relationship by fostering trust and understanding. Also, if her boyfriend's friend was lying, then her testing him could unnecessarily strain their relationship. It's important to consider the source of the information. If she doesn't know the friend well, it might be a case of someone trying to stir up drama. Without concrete evidence, it's risky to base her actions on hearsay. Furthermore, changing her behavior to test him might send the wrong message. It could imply that she's only with him for his interest in her looks, which is the opposite of what she wants. She wants someone who appreciates her beyond her appearance, so testing him in this way might contradict that goal. In conclusion, while her intentions are understandable given her past experiences, testing her boyfriend in this manner might not be the best approach. It could lead to mistrust, manipulation, and unnecessary strain on the relationship. Instead, open communication and building trust through honesty might be a healthier way to address her concerns.
